written.description: Rules on whether an agent skill is malicious, with a model judge whose catch and false-positive rates are published against a labelled test set. A team picks a policy and suppresses known findings, so the same skill gets the same verdict on every run.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix: close silent-skip paths in the scanner and two quadratic rules (#265)

* loader: stop skipping files under .git directories

_discover_files dropped every file with a .git path component, so a payload
placed in .git/ or scripts/.git/ never reached any analyzer and the scan
returned SAFE. Discover them like other hidden content.

* rules: keep eval comment exclude linear on long lines

The COMMAND_INJECTION_USER_INPUT exclude pattern "#.*eval" is quadratic
on a single long line, so a few hundred KB without a newline stalled a
scan for tens of seconds. Anchor it at the first '#' so it matches the
same lines in linear time.

* rules: keep ransomware chain identifier match linear on long lines

The identifier branch of MALWARE_RANSOMWARE_IMPLEMENTATION_CHAIN retried
every start offset inside a long identifier run, so one long line in a .py
file took minutes to scan. Require the identifier to start at a word
boundary; the same matches are found in linear time.

* scanner: report skills that fail to load as a HIGH finding in scan-all

scan_directory only logged load errors (invalid UTF-8 or symlinked SKILL.md)
and listed them under skills_skipped, so SARIF, markdown and the exit code
treated the unanalyzed skill as clean. Emit a SKILL_LOAD_FAILED finding for
it, like the existing size-limit rejection.

* cli: fail scan-all severity gate when a skill was skipped

A skill whose analysis crashed was listed under skills_skipped but the exit
code only looked at severity counts, so --fail-on-severity returned 0 with the
skill never scanned. Treat any skipped skill as a gate failure.

* api: reject scan-upload archives that hold several skills

scan-upload scanned whichever SKILL.md rglob returned first and reported
that result for the whole archive, so a benign skill placed first hid a
malicious one. Archives with more than one independent skill root now get
a 400; a SKILL.md nested inside another skill's directory still counts as
part of that skill.

* static: scan every frontmatter value and comment for prompt injection

Only description and when_to_use reached the text rules, so a payload in
license, metadata, extra keys or a YAML comment scanned as safe. Scan all
frontmatter text except allowed-tools, which holds tool-permission syntax.

* loader: report symlinks inside a skill instead of dropping them

File discovery skipped every symlink without a trace, so a payload behind a
symlink (file or directory, inside or outside the skill) was never scanned and
the result was SAFE. Symlinks are still not followed, but the loader now
records each one and the scanner emits a SYMLINK_NOT_SCANNED finding (HIGH when
the target is outside the skill root, MEDIUM otherwise).

* style: apply ruff format to new scanner and test code

* loader: keep skipping .git directories

Skipping .git inside a skill is intended: it holds version-control metadata, not skill content, and the hidden-files policy decides the other dot-directories. Reverts cb588ac.

* rules: declare the MEDIUM demotion for in-skill symlinks

SYMLINK_NOT_SCANNED emits MEDIUM for a symlink that stays inside the skill, but the pack only declared HIGH, so every such scan failed the rule contract and listed skill_loader as a failed analyzer.

* scanner: run load failures through the rule contract and suppressions

SKILL_LOAD_FAILED skipped the contract check, scoped suppressions and CEL that the size-limit rejection already goes through, so its policy knobs had no effect.

* static: scan inline comments on excluded frontmatter fields

The frontmatter view blanked whole lines of excluded fields such as allowed-tools, so a payload in an inline comment after the value was never scanned. Keep the comment, drop only the value.

* style: ruff format the new tests

* tests: review the SYMLINK_NOT_SCANNED severity demotion

Add the rule to the reviewed dynamic-severity and allowed-demotion lists, matching the pack declaration.
